description: Census of BS/MD and combined BS/MD-equivalent programs: the AAMC Official Guide listings (2025-2026 edition, with the 2026-2027 chapter checked) plus direct-entry and early-assurance routes the AAMC list does not carry, each verified on the institution's official pages. One entry per medical school. Figures carry per-field sources; figures a program does not publish are marked needs_verification, never estimated.
refresh_cycle: annual (rebuild before each admissions cycle; incremental refresh only)
schema_note: Each field with 'status': 'verified' was confirmed via web research with a cited source. Fields with 'status': 'needs_verification' are not yet researched and must be filled by Scholar on first relevant query, per the lookup-before-build protocol. City/state and program duration come directly from the AAMC guide and general institutional knowledge (stable facts), so they are populated for all institutions. Cutoffs, GPA, fees, and acceptance rates change annually and require live verification.

programs.university: Warren Alpert Medical School of Brown University (PLME)
programs.college_department: Program in Liberal Medical Education (PLME), Brown University College

in_state_preference.value: No — private institution, national/international applicant pool
in_state_preference.source: Wikipedia: Program in Liberal Medical Education

floor_sat.value: No published minimum. PLME's official average for matriculants is SAT ERW 742 and SAT Math 770 (a combined average of about 1512), reported as the average over the past 3 years on PLME's Facts & Figures page — an average of enrolled students, not a floor or a middle-50% range

floor_act.value: No published minimum. PLME's official average ACT Composite for matriculants is 34, reported as the average over the past 3 years on PLME's Facts & Figures page — an average of enrolled students, not a floor or a middle-50% range
floor_act.source: Brown University, Program in Liberal Medical Education — Facts & Figures https://plme.med.brown.edu/about/facts-figures

expected_gpa.value: Unweighted ~3.8+ recommended; no official minimum disclosed

programs.university: University of Alabama at Birmingham Marnix E. Heersink School of Medicine
programs.college_department: Early Medical School Acceptance Program (EMSAP) - undergraduate study at the University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB) in partnership with the UAB Marnix E. Heersink School of Medicine

in_state_preference.value: Restricted by high school location and in-state preferred: applicants must have attended an Alabama high school or a high school in a contiguous state (Florida, Georgia, Tennessee, Mississippi), and must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents. Within that pool EMSAP prefers Alabama students - UAB's EMSAP FAQ states about two-thirds of those admitted are from Alabama.
in_state_preference.source: UAB Heersink School of Medicine, Early Medical School Acceptance Program https://www.uab.edu/medicine/home/admissions/special-programs/emsap and UAB EMSAP Frequently Asked Questions https://www.residency.peds.uab.edu/students/academics/emsap/faq

floor_sat.value: 1360 minimum (published eligibility minimum). Admitted students average far higher: UAB's EMSAP FAQ reports the Class of 2020 academic average was 1470 SAT.
floor_sat.source: UAB Heersink School of Medicine, Early Medical School Acceptance Program https://www.uab.edu/medicine/home/admissions/special-programs/emsap and UAB EMSAP Frequently Asked Questions https://www.residency.peds.uab.edu/students/academics/emsap/faq

floor_act.value: 30 minimum composite ACT (published eligibility minimum). Admitted students average far higher: UAB's EMSAP FAQ reports the Class of 2020 academic average was 33 ACT.
floor_act.source: UAB Heersink School of Medicine, Early Medical School Acceptance Program https://www.uab.edu/medicine/home/admissions/special-programs/emsap and UAB EMSAP Frequently Asked Questions https://www.residency.peds.uab.edu/students/academics/emsap/faq

expected_gpa.source: UAB Heersink School of Medicine, Early Medical School Acceptance Program https://www.uab.edu/medicine/home/admissions/special-programs/emsap and UAB EMSAP Frequently Asked Questions https://www.residency.peds.uab.edu/students/academics/emsap/faq

annual_fees.value: Undergraduate phase at UAB, AY 2025-2026: tuition $11,640/year for Alabama residents (in-state) and $28,980/year for out-of-state students, plus $500/year in required fees (food and housing on campus listed separately at $13,240/year).
annual_fees.source: University of Alabama at Birmingham Common Data Set 2024-2025 (Section G, 2025-2026 costs), hosted at UAB https://www.ccts.cme.uab.edu/institutionaleffectiveness/images/documents/cds/CDS-2024-25.pdf

acceptance_rate.value: About 5% (secondary-source computation from program-reported counts: 339 applicants in 2024 - 54 Alabama, 285 out of state - with 17 accepted and 12 matriculated). UAB's own EMSAP FAQ reports over 400 completed applications in a typical year and up to 36 interview invitations for the medical program; UAB does not publish an official acceptance-rate percentage.
acceptance_rate.source: Oriel Admissions, Easiest BS/MD Programs to Get Into (rate computed from program-reported 2024 counts) https://orieladmissions.com/easiest-bs-md-programs/ ; corroborating applicant/interview volumes in UAB EMSAP Frequently Asked Questions https://www.residency.peds.uab.edu/students/academics/emsap/faq

programs.university: University of California, San Francisco, School of Medicine
programs.college_department: SJV PRIME+ BS/MD Program (San Joaquin Valley Program in Medical Education+) - a partnership between the University of California, Merced (undergraduate), UCSF Fresno, and the University of California, San Francisco, School of Medicine

in_state_preference.value: Strong regional restriction in practice: the program is designed for San Joaquin Valley-based high school students, and UC Merced's official admissions criteria state that holistic review considers applicants who 'are residents of and have deep ties to the San Joaquin Valley' (defined as nine counties: San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Mariposa, Fresno, Kern, Kings, and Tulare). It is not open as a general national BS/MD; only first-time freshman applicants applying directly to UC Merced in a qualifying major are reviewed.
in_state_preference.source: UC Merced Undergraduate Admissions, SJV PRIME+ Admissions Criteria and Application Process https://admissions.ucmerced.edu/node/5591

floor_sat.value: No SAT floor and no SAT considered: University of California admissions is test-free, and the SJV PRIME+ official criteria list no SAT requirement - eligibility rests on UC admission criteria and a minimum overall UC GPA of 3.6 in a qualifying major.
floor_sat.source: UC Merced Undergraduate Admissions, SJV PRIME+ Admissions Criteria and Application Process https://admissions.ucmerced.edu/node/5591

floor_act.value: No ACT floor and no ACT considered: University of California admissions is test-free, and the SJV PRIME+ official criteria list no ACT requirement - eligibility rests on UC admission criteria and a minimum overall UC GPA of 3.6 in a qualifying major.
floor_act.source: UC Merced Undergraduate Admissions, SJV PRIME+ Admissions Criteria and Application Process https://admissions.ucmerced.edu/node/5591

expected_gpa.value: Minimum overall UC GPA of 3.6 (high school, UC-calculated) required to apply; UC Merced notes competitive applicants should present a profile 'much stronger than any minimum UC admission requirements.' Continuation to UCSF School of Medicine requires a minimum cumulative and BCPM GPA of 3.6 by end of year 3 (3.7 for students entering the baccalaureate portion in Fall 2026 or later) and graduation from UC Merced within 4 years.
expected_gpa.source: UC Merced Undergraduate Admissions, SJV PRIME+ Admissions Criteria and Application Process https://admissions.ucmerced.edu/node/5591 ; UC Merced Medical Education, SJV PRIME+ Requirements for Acceptance to UCSF School of Medicine https://meded.ucmerced.edu/bs-md-pathway/student-handbook/student-progress/SOM-Acceptance-Requirements

annual_fees.value: Undergraduate phase at UC Merced, AY 2025-2026 total tuition and mandatory fees (without health insurance, entering 2025-26 cohort): $16,271/year for California residents and $53,873/year for nonresidents. UC Merced's SJV PRIME+ FAQ confirms the undergraduate cost aligns with the standard UC Merced cost of attendance, with no additional program cost.
annual_fees.source: University of California Office of the President, Total Charges 2025-26 by Campus https://www.ucop.edu/operating-budget/_files/fees/202526/2025-26-total-charges-by-campus.pdf ; UC Merced Undergraduate Admissions, BS to MD Frequently Asked Questions https://admissions.ucmerced.edu/faq-BS-to-MD

acceptance_rate.value: No percentage rate or applicant count published. UC Merced's official FAQ states the program currently admits 12 students per year (UCSF Fresno's program history reports 15 students per cohort in the inaugural 2023 cohort and in subsequent early cohorts).
acceptance_rate.source: UC Merced Undergraduate Admissions, BS to MD Frequently Asked Questions https://admissions.ucmerced.edu/faq-BS-to-MD ; UCSF Fresno, UCSF Fresno and UC Merced Provide a Pathway from High School to Medical School https://fresno.ucsf.edu/ucsf-fresno-and-uc-merced-provide-pathway-high-school-medical-school

programs.notes: Note (verified 2026-11-19): the BS/MD pathway is SJV PRIME+ (est. 2023) — undergraduate phase at UC Merced and medical training at UCSF Fresno; students do not study in San Francisco. Designed for students with ties to the nine-county San Joaquin Valley.

programs.notes: NAME CHANGE: the former Special Consideration Program (SCP) for Medicine is now the Mercer Medical Scholars Program (the School of Medicine's 2025-2026 catalog states this expressly: 'previously known as the Special Consideration Program'). High-school direct entry: students apply in the fall of the senior year after receiving an undergraduate offer from Mercer (Macon campus), with a complete application due mid-January, interviews in early February, and up to 60 invited to interview. TWO pathways in one program: (1) Standard Mercer Medical Scholars, 4 years undergraduate + 4 years MD (8 years total): any eligible undergraduate major, bachelor's degree awarded before medical school, MCAT required, apply via AMCAS Early Decision after the junior year, medical-school interview waived if all requirements are met. (2) Accelerated Mercer Medical Scholars, 3 years undergraduate + 4 years MD (7 years total): Biology or Biochemistry & Molecular Biology majors in the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences only, Calculus I readiness required, maintain 3.5 GPA, apply via AMCAS Early Decision after the sophomore year, NO MCAT required if all requirements are met, and the B.S. in Biomedical Sciences is awarded after successful completion of the first year of medical school (so accelerated students enter the MD phase before the bachelor's is conferred, but the degree is required and conferred during the MD phase; bs_required is therefore true). programs.notes: High-school direct entry, Tennessee residents only, for incoming MTSU freshmen (current application is for Fall 2027 entry; MTSU's published deadline pattern is December 1). Accelerated 7-year structure: 3 years of a prescribed undergraduate premedical curriculum at MTSU (Murfreesboro) + 4 years of medical school at Meharry (Nashville). Students receive conditional acceptance to Meharry's School of Medicine on matriculation into MSEAP, pending stated benchmarks: a mandatory two-week Bridge Program the summer before freshman year (split between MTSU and Meharry, free to students), a six-week summer academic and clinical enrichment program at Meharry each summer after the first MTSU year, an intense formal MCAT review with the MCAT taken and scores released to Meharry before matriculation (the MTSU page publishes no numeric MCAT minimum), and AMCAS plus Meharry applications. On the bachelor's degree: the MTSU catalog states the program lets students complete both a B.S. from MTSU and the M.D. from Meharry in seven years, and the MSEAP upper-division form defines the 120-hour B.S. as a minimum of 90 hours on the MTSU transcript plus completion of the professional program — i.e., students enter Meharry after three years and the B.S. is completed in conjunction with the professional program, so the degree is required and conferred during the MD phase (bs_required true). MISSION AND SERVICE COMMITMENT — counselors must flag this: the program exists to produce primary care physicians for rural and medically underserved Tennessee, and MTSU's own news reporting states participants owe a primary care residency in a rural/underserved area of Tennessee plus a post-residency service commitment (reported variously as two to three years; confirm the current obligation in the program agreement before applying). Funding: MTSU News reports selected students receive full tuition and fees paid by the program at both MTSU and Meharry, but the application page cautions that the up-to-10 annual seats are contingent upon funding, so verify funding for the entering year.

programs.notes: Naming: the medical school's current official name is the Texas A&M University Naresh K. Vashisht College of Medicine (used on its own early-assurance page); it was formerly the Texas A&M University College of Medicine. Structure: this is an early-assurance pathway into EnMed, not a conventional BS/MD. Students complete a full undergraduate engineering degree at Texas A&M in College Station (in the College of Engineering Honors environment), then transition to EnMed in Houston (Texas Medical Center, with Houston Methodist Hospital), where they earn both the MD and a Master of Engineering in four years — eight years total. City/state in this record are the medical school's home (Bryan, Texas); the EnMed medical phase itself is delivered in Houston. Two entry points: (1) high-school seniors who are National Merit Scholar semifinalists/finalists planning to enroll in the College of Engineering – College Station, and (2) current Texas A&M College of Engineering sophomores; transfer students are not eligible. Important counselor caution: Texas A&M's own EnMed page states that students who complete all program requirements are 'guaranteed for interview' for EnMed — final EnMed admission still requires the interview and a College of Medicine admissions offer, so this is conditional early assurance, not an unconditional guaranteed seat. No official SAT/ACT floor could be verified (the operative high-school screen is National Merit semifinalist/finalist status, which implies very high PSAT/SAT performance, but no numeric SAT/ACT minimum is published on the official pages reviewed), and no program-wide acceptance rate or cohort size is published officially (the Brown Foundation states up to 15 of its Brown Scholar E2EnMed candidates may matriculate to EnMed each year, which is a partner-specific figure, not a published total cohort size), so those fields are needs_verification.
